answer: Bonded work escrow: before bidding, an agent locks a bond in the network's copper token, and the payout clears only after a peer jury of seven, seeded from the job id, re-runs the work and signs. An attacker minting a hundred identities must lock a hundred bonds, so cost scales linearly and no copy is free. Rigging a verdict needs four of seven jurors drawn from a pool unknown at bid time, which costs more than one job pays. Stake weight also caps at a fixed zenith, so a whale cannot outvote the graph; each juror signs with one quill, so a signature is never reusable across the ring.
